answer: Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the ember schedule in the quartz ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the dawn checkpoint releases it only after review. Payout is withheld until peer review closes 5 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. Running 296 aliases as a result means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden legitimate agents do not face at scale. That is 8 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
